The specimen is received fresh for intraoperative consultation labeled with 
 the patient's name, hospital number and as "left thyroid lobe".  The specimen 
 consists of a 11.5 gm lobe of the thyroid measuring 5.5 x 2.7 x 2.5 cm.  A 
 long suture designates the isthmus and a short suture designates the superior 
 pole.  The outer surface is inked black serially sectioned and on cut surface 
 there is a 1.5 x 1 x 0.5 cm cyst lined with smooth lining and filled with 
 yellow-brown serous fluid in the distal pole.  Additionally there is a 0.5 
 tan-brown nodule centrally located.  Portions of the cyst and nodule are 
 submitted for frozen section and the remainder of the cryoblock is submitted 
 in cassette "FS1A".  Additional unfrozen representative sections are submitted 
 in cassette "1B-1D".

The specimen is received in formalin, labeled with the patient's name, 
 hospital number and as "right thyroid lobe."  The specimen consists of an 
 incompletely bisected thyroid gland.  The specimen measures 3.5 x 4.5 x 1.5 
 cm.  The outer surface is covered with white serosa.  The outer surface of the 
 specimen is inked black.  The specimen is serially sectioned.  The cut surface 
 is homogeneous, soft and shows two small light tan areas.  No other gross 
 lesions or nodularities were identified. Representative sections were obtained 
 and submitted in cassettes "1A" thru "1J".

The specimen is received in three parts.  Specimens #1-2 are received fresh
 for intraoperative consultation and specimen #3 is received in formalin, each
 labeled with the patient's name and hospital number.

Specimen #1 is labeled "pretracheal lymph node."  The specimen consists of one
 piece of fibroadipose tissue, measuring 1.5 x 1.0 x 5.0 cm.  There are three
 small lymph nodes that are dissected, each measuring approximately 0.2 x 0.1 x
 0.1 cm.  The specimen is submitted entirely for frozen section.  The frozen
 section is resubmitted for permanent section in cassette "1A."

Specimen #2 is labeled "right thyroid lobe and isthmus."  The specimen
 consists of a piece of thyroid measuring 5.3 x 3.3 x 1.8 cm and weighing 13.3
 grams.  There are two nodules, one measures 3.0 x 2.0 x 1.0 cm.  It is tan
 with focal hemorrhage.  The other nodule is ovoid with tan-white fibrous
 capsule and measures 0.4 cm in diameter.  A representative piece of the large
 lesion is submitted for intraoperative consultation and frozen section
 diagnosis and the remainder of the cryoblock is submitted in cassette
 "FS2A."  The entire specimen is submitted from superior to isthmus in
 cassettes "2B" through "2K."

Specimen #3 is labeled "left thyroid lobe."  The specimen consists of a piece
 of thyroid measuring 4.3 x 2.5 x 1.5 cm.  The specimen is multinodular and
 cystic throughout the entire specimen.  The entire specimen is submitted from
 superior to inferior in cassettes "3A" through "3G" with the isthmus in 
 casette.

Specimen #1 labeled "thyroid gland" consists of a thyroid gland with a single
 suture marking the isthmus and a double suture marking the right upper lobe,
 weighing 34.3 gm and measuring 8.0 x 3.5 x 3.5 cm.  The surface is
 nodular-appearing, and on cut section, there is a tan, lobular, soft,
 gelatinous cut section with focal areas of hemorrhage consistent with
 multinodular goiter.  A section is taken for frozen section evaluation and the
 remainder of the cryoblock is submitted in cassette "FS1A."  Additional
 sections are submitted as detailed in the cassette summary below.  The
 specimen was sectioned at 2-3 mm intervals and examined by Dr. Fischer.

Specimen #2 labeled "intrathoracic goiter" consists of a large, irregular,
 lobulated mass of tissue, weighing 35.6 gm and measuring 5.5 x 4.5 x 3.0 cm.
 The cut surface shows irregular nodular, gelatinous, tan-green to gray tissue
 with areas of cystic degeneration and nodules with peripheral calcification,
 consistent with multinodular goiter. Representative sections are submitted in
 cassettes "2A" through "2D."  Additional sections are submitted after
 sectioning at this interval and gross evaluation by Dr. Fischer. Additional
 sections are submitted as "2E" through "2M."

 Specimen #3 labeled "thymus" consists of a single fragment of fibroadipose
 tissue with focal areas of firm tissue.  The specimen is serially sectioned
 revealing fibroadipose tissue.  Representative sections are submitted in
 cassettes "3A" and "3B."  Subsequently, the remainder of this specimen is
 submitted in its entirety, (sections 3C,D and E).

Sections of the right lobe of thyroid show a well-differentiated classical invasive papillary carcinoma of the superior portion of the right lobe, measuring 1.6 cm in greatest dimension. The tumor demonstrates mixed papillary and follicular architectural
 features. There is a single small focus of early extrathyroidal tumor extension. In addition, there is a single minute focus of tumor involvement of the inked peripheral surgical margin of resection. No definite lymphovascular involvement or perineural
involvement by tumor is seen. A single small portion of a parathyroid gland is noted (examination of the immunohistochemical stains reveals positive staining for parathyroid hormone with negative staining for TTF-1 and thyroglobulin, consistent with
parathyroid gland tissue). No lymph nodes are identified within the submitted sections from the right lobe.

Sections of the left lobe of thyroid show a well-differentiated classical invasive papillary microcarcinoma of the midportion of the left lobe, measuring 0.3 cm in greatest dimension. The tumor demonstrates mixed papillary and follicular architectural
features. No extrathyroidal tumor extension is seen. The inked peripheral surgical margin of resection is negative for tumor. No definite lymphovascular involvement or perineural involvement by tumor is seen. A single 0.3 cm lymph node is identified,
demonstrating the presence of metastatic papillary carcinoma (no extranodal tumor extension is seen). No parathyroid glands are identified within the submitted sections from the left lobe.

Sections of the right lobe, isthmus, and left lobe of thyroid show a background of moderate chronic thyroiditis. Multiple benign adenomatoid nodules are identified, some of which show extensive calcification.

Sections of the 3.0 cm nodule removed from the left paratracheal space show mixed mature-appearing adipose tissue and thyroid follicles, consistent with a lipomatous lesion of the thyroid gland. No malignancy is seen.

MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION	The thyroid sections show scattered lymphoid aggregates with associated hyperplastic germinal centers. There is accompanying accentuation of thyroid lobules with some associated interlobular fibrosis. The thyroid follicles throughout tend to have a
somewhat uniform medium to sometimes small size. The thyroid follicles are generally colloid-filled with occasional scalloping of colloid and rare small papillary infoldings. Only in a few areas are the follicles in this thyroid lined by columnar
epithelium like expected with typical Grave's disease. There is accompanying vascular congestion. Note is made of the reported clinical history of Graves' disease, and the histologic findings, although not entirely classic, could be consistent with
Graves' disease.  Some of the histologic findings present could also be seen with Hashimoto's thyroiditis. Clinical correlation is suggested.

Identified in block A5 (from the left superior thyroid lobe), there is a 1.5 mm focus where small papillary fronds are surfaced by cells which display nuclear pallor, nuclear overlapping, small nucleoli, and occasional nuclear grooves (papillary
microcarcinoma).

The minute (less than 2 mm) benign lymph node is included in isthmus block A4.

No parathyroid glands are identified in any of the sections.

COMMENT SOFT CONVERSIONS	COMMENT BY DR. LUBIN (03/17/2020):  "The 3.5 cm mass which is represented in sections A1-A2, A13, and A15 through A23 demonstrates a relatively well-differentiated follicular neoplasm.  The cells demonstrate that nuclear features of papillary thyroid
carcinoma (nuclear enlargement, irregular nuclear membranes, and vesicular chromatin with peripherally-oriented pinpoint nucleoli) and are arranged in a follicular/microfollicular architecture with numerous foci of solid growth.  These areas of solid
growth lack increased mitoses or necrosis.  Rare true papillae with fibrovascular cores are appreciated.  Given the presence of true papillae in conjunction with the nuclear features, the lesion is best classified as a conventional papillary thyroid
carcinoma.  While a solid variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma could be considered, per 2017 WHO guidelines, this diagnosis should be relegated to lesions with "all or nearly all" of the tumor showing a solid, trabecular or nested appearance.  Another
diagnostic consideration would be a follicular variant of papillary thyroid carcinoma, however there are too many true papillae in this lesion to warrant that diagnosis.  No lymphovascular or perineural invasion are identified in the submitted sections,
and the lesion appears to be confined to the thyroid gland.
The additional 0.7 cm lesion also demonstrates a follicular lesion with nuclear features of papillary thyroid carcinoma as well as true papillae with fibrovascular cores, consistent with a papillary thyroid microcarcinoma.  While no lymphatic invasion is
 identified for either lesion, the possibility that this may represent a metastatic foci from the 3.5 cm mass rather than an additional primary also cannot be entirely excluded.
The background thyroid gland demonstrates multinodular hyperplasia, and a lymph node in section A16 is negative for carcinoma."
